title: Concerning a Man and Two Yakas
title_raw: CONCERNING A MAN AND TWO YAKAS
notes:
North-western Province.



In a variant in Folk-Tales of Bengal (Day), pp. 258-260, a barber
frightened a Bhuta (evil spirit) who was going to eat him, by
threatening to put him in his bag. He took out his looking-glass,
and showed the Bhuta his reflection, which the evil spirit thought was
another imprisoned one. The Bhuta promised to obey the barber's orders,
and provided money, and a granary filled with paddy. The Bhuta's uncle
told him that he had been cheated; but he was treated in the same way,
and made to build another granary, and fill it with rice.
text:
In a certain country there was a man who had cut a chena. The man,
without any one joining with him, went one day and made ready to cut
a fresh chena at a place where there was a large tree.

Then the Yaka who dwelt in the tree became afraid, and having descended
to the ground, and having said, "Lord, do not cut a chena here. At
every eventide I will bring and give you rice, coconuts, chillies,
etc.," he made obeisance. The man said, "It is good," and went home.

That very evening the Yaka brought and gave him rice and all things
sufficient for curries, and went away. After that, in no long time
the man became in a good position and wealthy, through the Yaka's
bringing him his provisions.

When coming afterwards, the Yaka met another Yaka, who asked, "Where
are you taking those things?"

The Yaka replied, "A man came to cut the residence in which I stay. On
account of it, I promised to give him food and goods."

Then the Yaka said, "Do thou give the things to-day only. I will kill
the man to-morrow."

The other Yaka said, "It is good."

On the following day, when the man of that house was going somewhere
or other, the Yaka who said, "I will kill him," came to the house,
and having crept under the bed remained there. At that time the man
returned, and sitting on the bed, said to his wife, "Bola, I am hungry
enough to eat a Yaka."

His wife had placed the knife on the shelf, and having plucked a
pine-apple had put it under the bed. The woman [not seeing the Yaka],
said, "Look there! On the shelf. Look there! Under the bed."

So the man, taking the knife that was on the shelf, went near the
bed to get the pine-apple. Then the Yaka, thinking he was coming to
kill and eat him, said, "Lord, do not eat me. I will bring and give
you each month anything you want."

So the man saying, "It is good," sent away the Yaka.

Then the Yaka met that other Yaka, and said, "When I went to set you
free I also was caught. Both of us are in the same state."

After that he gave the things monthly. Then this man having become
a great wealthy person, remained so.

ある国に、焼畑を切り拓いた男がいた。その男は、誰の力も借りずに、ある日、大きな木のある場所で新しい焼畑を切り拓く支度をした。
するとその木に棲むヤカー(鬼神)が恐れて地に下り、「旦那さま、ここで焼畑を切り拓かないでください。毎晩、米も椰子も唐辛子も、何もかも持ってきて差し上げますから」と言って、頭を下げた。男は「よろしい」と言って家へ帰った。
その晩さっそく、ヤカーは米と汁物に足りるものを何もかも持ってきて渡し、去っていった。それからほどなく、ヤカーが食べ物を運んでくるおかげで、男は身代のよい裕福な者になった。
そのあと運んでくる途中で、ヤカーは別のヤカーに出会い、こう尋ねられた。「そのものをどこへ運んでいる?」
ヤカーは答えた。「ある男が、わたしの棲みかを切り拓きに来た。そのために、食べ物と品物を差し上げると約束したのだ」
するとそのヤカーは言った。「その品を渡すのは今日かぎりにしろ。明日、わたしがその男を殺してやる」
もう一方のヤカーは「それがよい」と言った。
翌日、その家の男がどこかへ出かけていたとき、「殺してやる」と言ったヤカーが家へ来て、寝台の下に潜り込んでいた。そこへ男が帰ってきて、寝台に腰かけ、女房に言った。「ボラ、ヤカーでも食えるほど腹が減った」
女房は小刀を棚に置いていて、鳳梨をもいで寝台の下に入れてあった。女は〔ヤカーに気づかずに〕言った。「そこにありますよ! 棚の上に。そこにありますよ! 寝台の下に」
そこで男は棚の上の小刀を取って、鳳梨を取りに寝台のそばへ寄った。するとヤカーは、自分を殺して食べに来るのだと思って言った。「旦那さま、わたしを食べないでください。毎月、何でもお望みのものを持ってきて差し上げますから」
そこで男は「よろしい」と言って、ヤカーを帰した。
するとヤカーはもう一方のヤカーに出会って言った。「おまえを助けに行ったら、わたしも捕まってしまった。二人とも同じありさまだ」
そのあとヤカーは毎月品を渡した。そしてこの男はたいそう裕福な者となって、そのまま暮らしたのである。
